method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a seat-neutral core (jcxv-core.l4, one regulative rule for the s 6(5)(b) notice, two date helpers on the stable prelude, no daydate import, no YMD) and a seat layer (jcxv-seat.l4) that restates no rule; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Jurisdiction of Courts (Cross-vesting) Act 1987 (Qld) (act-1987-088), the version in force from 2011-01-01, current on 6 November 2026, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-1987-088.txt. Not deposited and asked as facts: the Commonwealth Jurisdiction of Courts (Cross-vesting) Act 1987 (special federal matter, its Schedule), the ADJR Act enactment paragraphs, the listed Australian Consumer Law provisions, Corporations Act part 9.6A division 1, Family Law Act s 41 proclamations.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run jcxv-core.l4 ; l4 run jcxv-seat.l4 ; l4 run jcxv-cases-party.l4
checks.result: 110 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-11-07, after the s 3(2) and s 6(9) fix); 2 #TRACEs with an expect line (FULFILLED; BREACH by the directed party), both as expected
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: The whole operative Act from the seat of the party: s 3 (definitions used), s 3A, s 4, s 5(1)-(4), (6)-(8), s 6(1)-(9), s 6A(1)-(3), s 7, s 8(1), (3), s 9, s 10, s 11(1), (3), s 12, s 13, s 14(1). Out: ss 1-2, 16, 17 (machinery, suspension, transitional saving), s 5(9) and s 6A(4)-(6) (interpretive limits), s 6(5)(a), s 6(6) (what the court weighs), s 8(2) (reflected, not separately asked), s 11(1)(c) (stated only), s 14(2) (interpretive), the preamble.
seat: the party to a civil proceeding (plaintiff, defendant, applicant, respondent, or a person who intervenes) whose proceeding touches Queensland and another Australian jurisdiction
